chunks: They said: "Have you come to turn us away from our gods? Then bring upon us what you predict for us, if you are a man of truth."

key_terms.آلِهَتِنَا: our gods (plural of ilah, referring to idols)
key_terms.تَأْفِكَنَا: to turn us away / to divert us

ai.seo_question: What did the polytheists say to Prophet Hud to challenge his prophecy?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Hud, the polytheists challenge Prophet Hud to produce the divine punishment he promised, revealing their arrogance and superficial understanding of prophetic authority. Shia scholarship often highlights this as a classic example of 'istikbar' (arrogance), where the elite demand immediate, tangible proof rather than accepting the spiritual truth of the message. This challenge underscores the recurring Quranic theme that disbelievers often test prophets to delay or dismiss the inevitable reality of divine retribution.
